Knowing the pattern side tells the remote pilot where manned aircraft will be flying, which helps comply with 14 CFR 107.43. RP does not mean private or closed.
explanation.keyTakeaway: RP on the chart = right-hand pattern for that runway. Know where the traffic will be.

stem: A remote pilot is surveying a lake shore next to a seaplane base marked on the chart. Does 14 CFR 107.43 apply?

choices.text: Yes; it covers seaplane bases, airports, and heliports alike
No; 107.43 covers only airports with paved runways
Yes, but only while a seaplane is on the water

explanation.correct: Yes; it covers seaplane bases, airports, and heliports alike.
explanation.reason: 14 CFR 107.43 prohibits operating a small unmanned aircraft in a manner that interferes with operations and traffic patterns at any airport, heliport, or seaplane base. Seaplanes take off from and land on the water, so their approach and departure paths over the lake are airport traffic the drone must not interfere with. 107.43 protects operations and traffic patterns, including seaplanes taking off and landing, not only aircraft on the water.
explanation.keyTakeaway: Seaplane bases are covered by 107.43, the same as airports and heliports.

stem: A drone flies at 350 feet AGL under the downwind leg of a non-towered airport's traffic pattern. A remote pilot reasons that propeller airplanes fly the pattern at 1,000 feet AGL, so there is no conflict. What does this overlook?

choices.text: Nothing; pattern traffic never comes below 1,000 feet AGL
Airplanes descend from late downwind; helicopters fly lower
Pattern altitude is 1,500 feet AGL for every aircraft

explanation.correct: Airplanes descend from late downwind; helicopters fly lower.
explanation.reason: AIM 4-3-3 says propeller-driven aircraft enter the traffic pattern at 1,000 feet AGL and maintain pattern altitude until abeam the approach end of the landing runway on the downwind leg, after which they descend to land, and that helicopters may fly the pattern at a lower altitude, about 500 feet AGL. The 1,500-foot figure applies only to large and turbine-powered aircraft. AC 107-2A, paragraph 5.10.1.2, says remote pilots should avoid the traffic pattern, and a drone never has priority over manned aircraft (14 CFR 107.37).
explanation.keyTakeaway: Pattern altitude is not a safe ceiling. Airplanes descend on late downwind, and helicopters fly lower.

stem: A remote pilot strikes a power line after misjudging how far away it was. Which causal factor on the AIM's list of the most frequent general aviation accident factors does this match?

choices.text: Misjudgment of distance and speed
Failure to maintain direction control
Selection of unsuitable terrain

explanation.correct: Misjudgment of distance and speed.
explanation.reason: AIM 7-6-1 lists the 10 most frequent causal factors for general aviation accidents involving the pilot in command, including misjudgment of distance and speed and failure to see and avoid objects or obstructions. Misjudging the distance to a power line matches misjudgment of distance. Failure to maintain direction control and selection of unsuitable terrain are also on the list but describe different failures.
explanation.keyTakeaway: Misjudging distance near obstacles is a classic accident factor. Give yourself margin.

stem: According to the AIM, if one aircraft inspects another in flight during an emergency, which pilot must not give up control of the situation?

choices.text: The pilot in command of the aircraft that has the problem
The pilot of the inspecting aircraft, who leads the maneuver
Whichever pilot has more flight experience

explanation.correct: The pilot in command of the aircraft that has the problem.
explanation.reason: AIM 7-6-11 says the pilot in the best position to assess the situation should coordinate the airborne inspection, and that the pilot in command of the aircraft experiencing the problem must not relinquish control of the situation or jeopardize the safety of that aircraft. It calls close-proximity in-flight inspection uniquely hazardous. For a drone, 14 CFR 107.37(b) prohibits flying so close to another aircraft as to create a collision hazard.
explanation.keyTakeaway: In an airborne inspection, the troubled aircraft's pilot stays in command of the situation.

stem: According to the AIM, what is the proper way to reduce precipitation static on an aircraft?

choices.text: Fly faster through the precipitation to shed the charge
Enough quality static dischargers, installed on a bonded airframe
Turn off the radios until the aircraft is clear of the clouds

explanation.correct: Enough quality static dischargers, installed on a bonded airframe.
explanation.reason: AIM 7-6-12 says precipitation static problems can only be corrected with the proper number of quality static dischargers, properly installed on a properly bonded aircraft, and that the dischargers need periodic maintenance. Speed and switching off radios do not remove the charge.
explanation.keyTakeaway: P-static is fixed with static dischargers on a bonded airframe.

stem: When a laser illumination of an aircraft is reported to an air traffic facility, what does the AIM say happens next?

choices.text: Cautions go out on frequency for 20 minutes and on ATIS for 1 hour
The airport closes until police locate the laser operator
Nothing; reports are only filed for later investigation

explanation.correct: Cautions go out on frequency for 20 minutes and on ATIS for 1 hour.
explanation.reason: AIM 7-6-13 says that when a laser event is reported to an air traffic facility, a general caution warning is broadcast on all appropriate frequencies every five minutes for 20 minutes and on the ATIS for one hour after the report. A remote pilot monitoring a frequency may hear this caution. The AIM does not describe closing the airport.
explanation.keyTakeaway: Laser reports trigger cautions on frequency for 20 minutes and on ATIS for an hour.

stem: Which statement about lasers aimed at aircraft is supported by the AIM?

choices.text: They can impair vision miles away and even damage eyes
They are harmless unless the beam is red
They affect only aircraft flying above 10,000 feet MSL

explanation.correct: They can impair vision miles away and even damage eyes.
explanation.reason: AIM 7-6-13 says illumination from laser operations can create temporary vision impairment miles from the actual location and can produce permanent eye damage. It notes beams are generally blue-green but may be red, yellow, or white, and some are invisible. No color or altitude makes them harmless. A remote pilot or visual observer whose eyes are affected could lose sight of the drone.
explanation.keyTakeaway: Lasers can impair vision miles away. Any color can be dangerous.

stem: Before a night job, a remote pilot checks NOTAMs and finds none for a tall lighted tower near the site. Can the pilot be sure the tower's lights are working?

choices.text: Yes; a light outage is always announced by NOTAM right away
No; tower light outages are never reported by NOTAM
No; outage NOTAMs may lag, so watch for unlit obstructions anyway

explanation.correct: No; outage NOTAMs may lag, so watch for unlit obstructions anyway.
explanation.reason: AIM 7-6-4 says NOTAMs are issued for lighted structures with temporary light outages, but that some time may pass before the FAA is notified and the NOTAM is issued, so pilot vigilance is imperative. New obstructions may also not appear on current charts. Light outages are reported by NOTAM, but sometimes late.
explanation.keyTakeaway: NOTAMs help, but outages can go unreported for a while. Survey the site.

stem: According to the AIM, which kinds of information can a NOTAM give a remote pilot?

choices.text: Long-range weather forecasts for the coming week
Permanent airspace boundaries that never appear on charts
Temporary airspace, obstruction, or airport changes

explanation.correct: Temporary airspace, obstruction, or airport changes.
explanation.reason: AIM 5-1-3 says the NOTAM system gives pilots time-critical aeronautical information that is temporary, or information to be published on charts at a later date, and that NOTAMs can affect aerodromes, runways, obstructions, communications, airspace, and navigation aids. The NOTAM is cancelled when the information is charted or the condition returns to normal. Forecasts come from weather products, not NOTAMs.
explanation.keyTakeaway: NOTAMs carry temporary or not-yet-charted information. Weather forecasts come elsewhere.

stem: During a night job, a crew member shines a bright white flashlight around the launch area while the remote pilot watches the drone. What does the PHAK say about this?

choices.text: It helps, because bright light keeps the pilot alert at night
It does not matter, because night vision is unaffected by light
Bright light undoes dark adaptation, so keep lights dim

explanation.correct: Bright light undoes dark adaptation, so keep lights dim.
explanation.reason: The PHAK (FAA-H-8083-25C, Chapter 17) says the eyes take about 30 minutes to adapt fully to darkness and that exposure to bright light can undo that adaptation, and it recommends dim lighting to protect night vision. Chapter 2 recommends carrying a smaller flashlight that can be dimmed and kept nearby. Bright light does not improve alertness, and it does affect night vision.
explanation.keyTakeaway: At night, keep lights dim around the pilot to protect dark adaptation.

stem: A remote pilot sees spherical markers on overhead wires near a river crossing. What do they indicate?

choices.text: A boundary of controlled airspace
A wildlife refuge that drones must avoid
Overhead wires that may be hard to see

explanation.correct: Overhead wires that may be hard to see.
explanation.reason: AIM 7-6-4 says spherical markers may be used to identify overhead wires and catenary transmission lines and may be lighted, because overhead lines and their supporting structures may not be readily visible and the wires can be virtually impossible to see under some conditions. They do not mark airspace or wildlife areas.
explanation.keyTakeaway: Spherical markers mean wires. Expect more you cannot see.

stem: At night, within a few miles of an airport, a remote pilot sees a very bright, steady white light on an aircraft that seems to be heading toward the area. Based on the AIM, what is it most likely?

choices.text: A landing light, which pilots are urged to use near airports
An anti-collision light, which on aircraft must be green
A searchlight, which the AIM requires on all aircraft at night

explanation.correct: A landing light, which pilots are urged to use near airports.
explanation.reason: AIM 4-3-24 says pilots are encouraged to turn on their landing lights when operating below 10,000 feet, day or night, especially within 10 miles of any airport, so a bright, steady white light on an aircraft near an airport is most likely a landing light. The same paragraph says anti-collision systems use rotating beacons or strobes colored red or white, not green, and it requires position lights from sunset to sunrise, not searchlights.
explanation.keyTakeaway: A bright steady white light near an airport is usually a landing light. Expect the aircraft to be coming your way.

stem: A drone's built-in steady red and green arm LEDs can be seen about 1 statute mile away. It has no other lights. Is it equipped for a night flight under Part 107?

choices.text: Yes; any lights that show the drone's orientation meet the rule
No; it needs flashing anti-collision lighting visible 3 statute miles
No; it needs steady position lights visible for 5 statute miles

explanation.correct: No; it needs flashing anti-collision lighting visible 3 statute miles.
explanation.reason: 14 CFR 107.29(a)(2) requires a small unmanned aircraft operating at night to have lighted anti-collision lighting visible for at least 3 statute miles, with a flash rate sufficient to avoid a collision. Steady LEDs seen 1 statute mile away meet neither part of that rule. Part 107 sets no position-light requirement and no 5-mile standard; the manned-aircraft lighting rules in Part 91 do not apply to Part 107 aircraft (91.1(f)).
explanation.keyTakeaway: Night under Part 107: flashing anti-collision light, visible 3 SM. Orientation LEDs alone do not qualify.
